chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Amr ibn Thabit, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Allah, the Exalted, created Karbala twenty-four thousand years before He created the Ka'bah, sanctified it, and blessed it. So it remained sanctified and blessed before Allah created the creation, and it will remain thus, and He will make it the best land in Paradise.

key_terms.الْكَعْبَةَ: The Ka'bah, the cube-shaped building in Mecca

ai.seo_question: When was Karbala created relative to the Ka'bah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) highlighting Karbala's primordial sanctity, noting it was created and blessed 24,000 years before the Ka'bah. This tradition underscores the site's unique ontological status as the 'best land in Paradise,' reinforcing its centrality in Shia devotional geography and the spiritual merit of visiting Husayn (a.s.).

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 13. All of my scholars including my father and my brother narrated to me from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Ali, from Abī Sa’īd Al-‘Usfuri, from Abil Miqdām ‘Amr ibn Thābit, from his father, who said: Abū Ja’far (Imam Bāqir (a.s.)) said:

Allāh, the Exalted, created, blessed, and sanctified Karbalā twenty-four thousand years before He created the Ka’bah. Therefore, it was blessed and sanctified before the creation of any created being and it will remain this way. And Allāh will make it the best land in Paradise. It will be the best abode in Paradise in which Allāh will make His friends abide. The above Ḥadīth has also been narrated to me through the following chain: My father, my brother and ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain, from ‘Ali ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Ali, from Abī Sa’īd ‘Abbād Al-‘Usfuri, from Abil Miqdām ‘Amr ibn Thābit, from his father, from Abī Ja’far (a.s.).
